Why `apt-get install` version of programs are older than `configure make make install`?

I don't know the distribution you're referencing, but the apt-get install is likely from the package manager. The package managers job is to ensure that everything plays nice together, avoiding dependency issues. If you download the latest libreoffice, but your GTK version is not compatible, you now get to manually install the latest GTK which also may have its own dependencies. I believe the term used to be dependency hell.

Programs have to be tested to make sure they work well with the rest of the system. Once stable programs are found, they usually only get security/stability updates and generally not new feature updates. Here's a bit of info on how Ubuntu does it.

When you compile from source, you're normally compiling the most up to date code in the program's trunk branch.

If you want the latest versions of programs, you can compile them from source, change your installation to the current or testing release instead of stable (not recommended for most users), or you can change to a distribution that's more bleeding edge. Some distributions have a rolling release like Arch Linux, although packages sometimes break requiring downgrading to a previous version.

Edit: grammar

On a versioned distro, the maintainers freeze the version of packaged software for the sake of stability and consistency.

If you want the latest&greatest, you need a rolling release distro, like Gentoo or Arch. Do note, that these incur a higher cost of maintenance

You can compile older code too.

Debian comes in three branches; Stable, Testing and Unstable. Debian based distributions (ones using apt package manager) tend tho choose the Stable branch which gets the updates when everything is tested to work together with everything else. I'm sure you can switch out the branch somehow, but I haven't been a Debian user for 10+ years so don't blame me for not remembering how.
Make is 21 years older than apt so I don't get the question.
OP was asking why the versions of programs included with the distributions package manager are of an older version than those that can be compiled manually using make.
